retention.stated: One week old at time of research. Storage is leased time, so 'free 5 GB' and 'kept forever' are not the same claim.

egress.terms: Reads via the Console API/MCP; the underlying Walrus network serves blobs from storage nodes. No egress meter published.

tooling: Genuinely good for an agent workflow: API keys plus an MCP server that plugs into Claude Code, Codex and Cursor; 'Agent Storage Loop' SDK for batched small writes with durability confirmation. Encrypted by default, per-file on-chain fingerprint.
chaining: The paid path is buying WAL and paying per epoch (storage is leased in time units, not bytes-forever) — so cost scales with retention period × size, which is the opposite of an archive.
limits_note: fails-quota at 5 GB by two orders of magnitude. Retention is epoch-based, so data expires unless renewed — a retention-clamped model at the protocol level.

extras.agent_focus: 2026-era research-data and data-marketplace platforms, deliberately judged on the BINDING constraint (does a person with only an email get past the write gate?) rather than on the marketing quota. Coverage: IEEE DataPort (the wave-7 discovery this slot confirms and extends), Mozilla Data Collective (2025 launch, the only new ≥100 GB-per-file free host found), Source Cooperative re-probed at the byte level, the French national Dataverse (Recherche Data Gouv) as the one genuinely EU-funded space with a self-serve email account, plus the 2026 data-marketplace entrants (Snowflake, Databricks Free Edition, data.world, Datarade, Tableland, Spice.ai, DataChain), the EU Data Spaces (Gaia-X / Catena-X / EOSC EU Node / DICE) and ResearchGate/Academia.edu data upload. Two structural results dominate: (a) the 'data marketplace' category is uniformly not storage — they are catalogues, and every one of them fails on per-object size by two to three orders of magnitude; (b) the EU Data Spaces are real and large but gated on eduGAIN/eIDAS identity, so they are closed on identity exactly like CSC Allas and LUMI-O before them.
